records.title: Dispatch Loom
records.subtitle: Dispatch reconciliation tool · Harbor Tools
records.summary: Built an internal dispatch reconciliation tool for comparing the overnight spreadsheet with the daily export. Personally wrote the Python parser and SQL checks, gathered requirements from warehouse supervisors, and explained validation failures. Operators used visible warnings and kept empty rows visible; supervisors made final dispatch decisions. This was operational reconciliation work, not delivery-speed measurement.

decisions.reason: The profile summary and personal context are stated directly. Each listed denial is also explicitly supported by the source.
The employer, dates, role, personal tool-building and training work, and team-attributed reconciliation result are supported. The linked skills and achievements match the described work.
The summary says operators used visible warnings, but the source only says they preferred a visible warning when the source file arrived late. That turns a stated preference into an assertion of use.
The source states that Ada personally trained 12 dispatch coworkers in two workshops and wrote the handbook; it also says exact workshop dates are unavailable.
The time reduction, six-run measurement, team attribution, Ada's parser-and-checks contribution, coworkers' changed habits, and correction of the earlier 50% figure are supported.
The source explicitly says Ada wrote the Python parser herself, and places Python in the Data tools skill category.
The source explicitly says Ada wrote the SQL checks herself, and places SQL in the Data tools skill category.
The source says PostgreSQL was used for the production database and lists it in the Data tools skill category.
The source says Git was used for version control and lists it in the Collaboration skill category.
The source supports personal coworker training in two workshops and lists coworker training in the Collaboration skill category.
The degree, institution, and dates are stated directly in the source.
The certificate name and date are stated directly; the source also characterizes it as a course completion rather than a professional license.
